catalog_quote: As described in detail, the number of contrastive tones varies from DOM1 to DOM2. DOM1 involves a three-way contrast, i.e. /H/, /M/ and /L/ ... while DOM2 involves a two-way contrast, i.e. /H/ and /L/ ... Another prosodic property is what I call here “prominence”, which is involved in DOM1. Roots are always pronounced with certain auditory “prominence”, which non-roots lack. This prominence involves a relatively wide pitch range, as well as loudness and length. The wide pitch range is relevant to the discussion on tonal reduction in DOM2 in Section 2.4.2. Since the details concerning the phonetic nature of prominence is still to be investigated, systematic research must be conducted in future studies. [p.53] As I stated in Section 2.2.2.3, unlike DOM2, DOM1 is always pronounced with prominence. This prosodic feature of DOM1 involves a pitch range that is wider than that of DOM2. [p.93] Although this context is useful for demonstrating the phonetic manifestation of the tonal melodies, it may exaggerate the prominence of each token. In my auditory impression, prominence attenuates in running speech.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Gǀui is a tone language with two tonological domains: the bimoraic lexical root (DOM1) bears one of six melodies built from three tones (H, M, L) and is always produced with 'prominence' (wider pitch range, greater loudness and length); grammatical non-roots (suffixes, particles, clitics = DOM2, typically monomoraic) contrast only H vs L and lack prominence. I.e. stress-like prominence is morphologically fixed on the lexical root (word-initial in this suffixing language), not contrastive in position; the author does not call it 'stress'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed. Trimoraic morphological roots and derived words are analysed as DOM1 (first two morae, prominent) followed by DOM2 (third mora, non-prominent) (§2.4.3 pp.53ff).
new_statements.exceptions: Suffixal copies in productive reduplication fall into DOM2 (no prominence, reduced tone contrast) even though segmentally derived from roots (p.42); prominence attenuates in running speech and the citation-form elicitation may exaggerate it (p.93); the phonetic nature of prominence is explicitly left for future research (p.42). Pitch-range correlate measured: DOM1 mean 59.3 Hz vs DOM2 26.8 Hz across six male speakers, t=6.0, p<.01 (§2.7.4 p.102).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns lexical roots vs grammatical morphemes within the word, based on citation forms and short frame sentences; author notes prominence weakens in connected speech. No claim about phrase-level accent.
new_statements.identity_note: Nakagawa 2006 describes Gǀui proper (gwii1239) as spoken at Xade / New Xade (Central Kalahari Game Reserve relocation communities), with three dialectal varieties identified in Ch.1; comparative Gǁana (gana1274) data appear only in Ch.3-5. The same thesis files were first saved under by the Gǁana readers and are copied into gwii1239/ (identical bytes).

tone_statements.citation: 中川裕 [Nakagawa, Hirosi]. 2018. 声調交替のパラディグマティックな説明：グイ語における2つの畳語パラダイムの相互作用音韻史 [A paradigmatic explanation of tonal alternation: the interacting phonological history of two reduplication paradigms in Gǀui]. 日本言語学会第156回大会予稿集 (Proceedings of the 156th Meeting of the Linguistic Society of Japan, University of Tokyo, oral session 2018-06-23), paper C-7, pp. 135-138. 日本言語学会.
tone_statements.quote: 本研究は、そのような事例として、南部アフリカで話される声調言語であるグイ語（コイサン諸語コエ語族カラハリ・コエ語派）における、2種類の畳語プロセスに関与する声調交替を取り上げる。[...] グイ語の語根は２モーラからなり、次の６種類の声調メロディーのどれかを基底声調としてもつ：声調メロディー目録 {HH, HM, HL, MM, LL, LM}。これらの声調メロディーは形態論的プロセスにおいて交替することがある。その際の声調交替は目録の内部で起き、声調交替が６種類以外のメロディーを生み出すことはない。
tone_statements.translation: As such a case, this study takes up the tonal alternations involved in two reduplication processes of Gǀui (Khoisan: Khoe family, Kalahari Khoe branch), a tone language spoken in southern Africa. [...] A Gǀui root consists of two morae and has as its underlying tone one of the following six tonal melodies: melody inventory {HH, HM, HL, MM, LL, LM}. These tonal melodies may alternate in morphological processes; the alternation then takes place inside the inventory, and tonal alternation never produces a melody other than these six.

tone_statements.quote: There are four classes of bimoraic roots in terms of their syllabic structure, namely CV:, CVV, CVN and CVCV. For each class, I have identified six tonal melodies in G|ui. In order to represent the six melodies, I employ a decomposition analysis under which contour melodies are interpreted as sequences of two tones by postulating three tones, namely /H/ (High), /M/ (Mid) and /L/ (Low). As already discussed in Nakagawa (2006), the three postulated tones are necessary and sufficient for representing all the tonal contrasts and for adequately stating the tonological processes of G|ui.

sources.locator: Ch.2 Tonology, §2.2.2.3 'Comparison of DOM1 and DOM2 in terms of features', p.42 ( page 11); supporting: §2.4.2 p.53, §2.7.1 p.93, §2.7.4 p.102 and Table 2.3 p.43
sources.note: Tone language: bimoraic lexical roots (tonal domain DOM1) contrast three tones /H M L/ giving six melodies; grammatical non-roots (DOM2, mostly monomoraic) contrast only H vs L. Roots 'are always pronounced with certain auditory prominence, which non-roots lack', involving wide pitch range, loudness and length (§2.2.2.3 p.42; restated §2.4.2 p.53; pitch-range measurement §2.7.4 p.102; p.93 prominence attenuates in running speech). The word 'stress' is never used.

sources.note: First-hand acoustic-phonetic and phonological account of Gǀui lexical tone: bimoraic roots (CV:, CVV, CVN, CVCV) carry one of six tonal melodies, analysed with three level tones /H, M, L/ (level HH, MM, LL; contour HM, HL, LM), minimal sextuplet given; F0 tracks of the six melodies in isolation; two phonetics-phonology mismatches: phonologically level melodies surface with falling contours, and L carries redundant breathy voice enhancing the L/M contrast.
